summary: The most likely cause of the low oxygen condition (82% purity) is a leak or a failing sieve bed/compressor. First, inspect the device for external leaks and then measure the oxygen output with a calibrated analyzer.

steps.action: Ensure patient is on backup oxygen supply. Then inspect all external tubing, connectors, and humidifier bottle for visible signs of leaks, loose fittings, or moisture.
steps.expected: No hissing sound, no moisture, and all connections are secure.

cite.quote: • Verify that there are no leaks

steps.action: Ensure patient is on backup oxygen supply. Allow the unit to warm up for at least 10 minutes, set flow to 5 LPM, and measure oxygen purity at the outlet with a calibrated oxygen analyzer. (For OPI units only when device is alarming.)

cite.quote: If the device is alarming and the oxygen concentration is measured at 82% or higher, check the device for leaks.

steps.action: Switch off and unplug the concentrator. Ensure patient is on backup oxygen supply. Follow the Sieve Canister Assembly Replacement procedure in Section 8.10 of the manual, using a new approved part. Avoid handling molecular sieve material; return old canister to Respironics for disposal.
steps.expected: After replacement, oxygen purity reads ≥90% (or ≥87% for applicable models).
